<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/spec`, touching **17** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **6** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-defaults/ui.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/ui.json`, `packages/spec/liveness/view.json`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-5.mdx`  _(via retiredAfter (symbol, a field of const object personalViewDeclarationsRemoved), retiredFromLoadPath (symbol, a field of const object personalViewDeclarationsRemoved))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **6** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-defaults/ui.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/ui.json`, `packages/spec/liveness/view.json`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **7** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **216** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **156** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **156**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **101** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **168** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a644163669cc57d6d1471008caad6099f1f49413` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `b05c3ad60190f47bdc32d0357a0ea67208779d4a` — the merge of head `92ac574df7221a069c1a7047e0c29b1c008d69a5` into base `a644163669cc57d6d1471008caad6099f1f49413`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin b05c3ad60190f47bdc32d0357a0ea67208779d4a && git checkout b05c3ad60190f47bdc32d0357a0ea67208779d4a
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin a644163669cc57d6d1471008caad6099f1f49413 92ac574df7221a069c1a7047e0c29b1c008d69a5 && git checkout -B drift-repro a644163669cc57d6d1471008caad6099f1f49413 && git merge --no-ff 92ac574df7221a069c1a7047e0c29b1c008d69a5

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a644163669cc57d6d1471008caad6099f1f49413
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs a644163669cc57d6d1471008caad6099f1f49413` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 席位核对 — ACCEPT · `domain:spec#1` · head `92ac574d`

1. **Shape:** draft, base `main` (main `96fb7b5d` merged in), `Fixes #29037`, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` / `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` in the body and the changeset. 39 files, +975/-292. Not governed.
2. **Ruling:** #28971 letter C (6570568131, 「同意」) rules the narrowing. Both inert `personal` values retire with a prescription; `sharing.type` retires whole because the badge was its only reader (the PR states the reading).
3. **Surface:** claim 6578962562 as amended on this card. The ui emitter, the badge i18n keys, ui pins and the ADR-0087 retirement mechanics are forced by the key's retirement, and the seat accepts them.
4. **Open questions, the seat's answers:** `collaborative` is accepted and stripped as emitted residue (#12840): **A**. The identifier `personalViewDeclarationsRemoved` is kept, and the id string is unchanged: **A**.
5. **Readings (dev, on `92ac574d`):** spec 791 files / 23468 tests; check:generated 0; metadata-protocol 47/47; ui consumers 642/642; 110/110 derived gates, DERIVED zero. Dogfood 389/396: two control timeouts pass alone, and four flow reds come from main's #29365, which main's #29451 fixes (17/17 with its three files). CI runs on the merge ref, so it carries #29451.
6. **Landing:** a narrowing on the published schema face, so one `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` review by the seat (claim line follows). After a PASS and green CI, the seat readies and queues. Next on `view.zod.ts` is #28522.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `92ac574df7221a069c1a7047e0c29b1c008d69a5`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/conversions/registry.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/retired-keys/18.ui__ViewSharing__type.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.ui-view-personal-declarations-retired.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/registry.ts.template, packages/spec/src/ui/view.zod.ts, ui/packages/core/src/utils/normalize-list-view.ts, ui/packages/plugin-list/src/ListView.tsx + packages/spec/src/shared/retired-key.ts, packages/spec/src/conversions/walk.ts, packages/spec/src/conversions/types.ts, packages/spec/src/ui/assembled-views.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/ui/component.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/ui/view-personal-declarations-retirement.test.ts, packages/spec/src/shared/retired-key-removal-version.pin.test.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-metadata-issues.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-stored-item-conversion.ts, packages/metadata/src/loaders/database-loader.ts, ui/packages/plugin-list/src/__tests__/ListView.test.tsx, ui/packages/core/src/utils/__tests__/normalize-list-view.test.ts, ui/packages/react/src/hooks/useViewSharing.ts, .changeset/29037-view-personal-declarations-retired.md, .github/workflows/ci.yml

Inputs read: card #29037 (body, triage 6571434336, seat claim 6578962562, dev report 6582129886, claim amendment 6582177714), the ruling of record 6570568131 on #28971 (letter C, 「同意」), the PR body, its file list, `git diff origin/main...92ac574d` and the 66 check-runs on the head. The seat's conclusions were not adopted; every claim below was re-read in the tree.

### ① Derived judgments

**The accept-set narrowing — `scope: 'personal'`.** `ViewScopeSchema` is `enumWithRetiredValues(['package', 'shared'], VIEW_SCOPE_RETIRED)` (`view.zod.ts`); the helper refuses at construction a retired member still listed, a blank prescription, or no retired member, and answers `personal` with the prescription through the enum's own error map. Every door that reads a view item's `scope` derives from the two `ViewScopeSchema` reads at `view.zod.ts` (the strict record and the wire member): `ViewMetadataSchema`'s record and overlay arms and `AssembledViewArtifactSchema` build on those shapes, and the new test pins five doors plus `defineViewItem`. The union doors (`view` save door, assembled channel) report the refusal inside `invalid_union.errors`; `protocol-metadata-issues.ts` already descends `invalid_union` branches on the wire, so the HTTP author sees the prescription, not `Invalid input`. `package` and `shared` are kept and parsed through (CONTROL rows). `git grep` on the head: no writer of `scope: 'personal'` in `packages/`, `ui/`, `examples/`, `templates/`, `skills/`, `content/` outside the retirement kit; `ui/` has no reader of `scope` at all (the switcher groups by `viewKind` + `object`).

**`sharing.type` retires whole, as a tombstone.** `ViewSharingSchema` is `acceptRetiredDefaultResidue(strictObject({ type: retiredKey(VIEW_SHARING_TYPE_RETIRED), lockedBy }), { type: 'collaborative' })`. The tombstone carries the prescription (version `18.3.0`, what replaced it, the one-line fix, the `os migrate meta --from 17` sentence) and the TypeScript face is `never`; `personal`, `private` and any other value are refused with the tombstone's text at all six list-view doors the test pins (`ListViewSchema`, `view.list`, `view.listViews.*`, `ObjectListViewSchema`, a list item's `config`, the flattened list overlay), at the object door and at `defineStack` as `STACK_SCHEMA_INVALID` / 422. Retiring the key rather than narrowing it to one value is what the card's target 2 asked for once no reader beyond the badge needed it; the head confirms that reading: the one production reader of `sharing.type` on `main` was `ListView.tsx`, and `ui/packages/types` takes `ViewSharingSchema` by reference. The ruling names the `personal` declarations; the whole-key retirement is the card's conditional target, exercised with the reading stated in the PR body, so it is within what the card authorises.

**`collaborative` as residue (#12840).** `acceptRetiredDefaultResidue` strips the key only when its value equals the captured literal `'collaborative'`, copy-on-write, in a `z.preprocess` ahead of the closed shape; any other value falls through to the tombstone. This is exactly the house rule that helper encodes (a retired DEFAULTED key's emitted default is residue, not an authoring choice, discriminated by value because JSON carries no provenance). `main`'s schema had `.default('collaborative')`, so every artifact a released toolchain parsed with a `sharing` block carries that literal, and refusing it would strand every stored list view with a `sharing` block for nothing. The authoring face still rejects a fresh `type: 'collaborative'` at `tsc`. Sound.

**Nothing refused beyond ruling C and the card.** `scope: 'package' | 'shared'` and `sharing.lockedBy` are unchanged (CONTROL rows pass through by value). The form view's public-link `sharing` block is a different schema (`SharingConfigSchema`) and the D2 test proves it is untouched. `normalize-list-view.ts` no longer folds the legacy objectui `visibility`/`enabled` pair onto a `type`; it drops the pair and keeps `lockedBy`, which is the only change that could reach the Console's own normalisation and it invents no retired key.

**The D2 conversion covers every shape the narrowing newly refuses.** Newly refused stored shapes are (a) `scope: 'personal'` on a view item record or flattened overlay in `views` or the assembled `viewItems` channel, and (b) `sharing.type` on a list payload wherever a list payload can sit: a record's `config`, a container's `list` and `listViews.*`, a flattened list overlay, the same three in `viewItems`, and `objects[].listViews.*`. `personalViewDeclarationsRemoved` reaches (a) through `mapCollection` over both collections (containers skipped, which is right: no container shape ever declared `scope`), and (b) through `mapViewPayloads` (`walk.ts`: record `config`, container slots, flattened overlay, in that guarded order), an explicit `viewItems` pass with the same three spellings, and an `objects` pass over `listViews`. `component.zod.ts` lifts `columns`, `selection`, `rowActions`, `bulkActions`, `calendar`, `conditionalFormatting` off `ListViewSchema.shape` but never `sharing`, so no page block carries the key and the "no page block declares `sharing`" claim holds. The fixture exercises all eight paths and asserts `expectedNotices: 8`; the new test replays a stored record, a stored overlay and a stored container through `applyConversionsToStoredItem('view', …)` and parses the output through all four item schemas, proves idempotence (second replay returns the same reference) and proves the entry is retired from the authoring funnel. `applyConversionsToStoredItem` is the seam both `database-loader.ts` and `protocol-stored-item-conversion.ts` read stored rows through, so no stored view is stranded. `retiredFromLoadPath: true` with `retiredAfter: '18.2.0'` matches `types.ts` (a retired entry must carry the version it retired after) and the ten other 18.2.0 entries; the prescription's `18.3.0` is the version the `minor` changeset produces from `18.2.0`, which `retired-key-removal-version.pin.test.ts` now pins for both refusals. Order 82 is the highest in `MAJOR_18_CONVERSIONS` and nothing earlier in the chain produces either declaration (no other conversion touches a list `sharing` block; `viewItemOwnerHiddenRemoved` at 37 deletes `owner`/`hidden` and its bystander fixture row moved from `scope: 'personal'` to `'shared'` to keep whole-table replay disjoint). The `(removed)` route, deleting rather than writing `shared`, changes nothing a reader sees and matches the prescription's own instruction.

### ② Semver level

`Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` are the right lines: a value is refused and a key is tombstoned, nothing is added or re-meant. The PR body and the changeset carry both, identically. The changeset is `minor` on `@objectstack/spec`, `@object-ui/plugin-list`, `@object-ui/core` and `@object-ui/i18n`, the four published packages whose source the diff moves (the metadata-protocol, plugin-view, types and console edits are test-only), which is the "a kind takes at least `minor` on a package the diff moves" rule; it opens with a `feat(spec)!:` summary and a **BREAKING** banner, carries the FROM → TO mapping and the one-line fix, states the parse text, the residue rule and what is unchanged, and carries exactly one ADR-0087 marker, an HTML comment reading `adr-0087: registered view-personal-declarations-removed, ui-view-personal-declarations-retired`, in the comma-separated `registered` form `check-adr-0087-registration.mjs` documents; both ids resolve in the registries on the head (`MIGRATIONS_BY_MAJOR[18].conversionIds` and `.semantic`, pinned by the new test). `Check Changeset`, `Lint & Repo Gates` and the PR-body guards are green on the head.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Surface breach, all forced.** Everything outside the claim's named surface is either a pin of the removed key (ui `registry-inputs-spec-parity`, ListView/ListViewBlock, ObjectView protocol-keys, `p1-spec-alignment`, `protocol.graft-folded-form-sections`), the emitter and strings the badge removal makes dead (`normalize-list-view.ts` and its test; `list.sharingPersonal` / `list.sharingCollaborative` out of all ten locales, `list.sharingLockedBy` kept in all ten), or the ADR-0087 mechanics a tombstone requires (one `retired-keys` entry `ui/ViewSharing:type` in the `18.ui__Def__key.ts` form of its neighbours, one `semantic` entry named after its id, one STEP18 rationale fragment at order 117, `vitest.repo-tests.json`, the removal-version pin). The claim amendment 6582177714 accepts exactly this set. Nothing in the diff is outside it.
- **Open question A on `collaborative`:** sound, see ①. **Open question A on the identifier `personalViewDeclarationsRemoved`:** sound; the registry id string `view-personal-declarations-removed` is what every registry, notice, changeset marker and test reads, and the TypeScript identifier is file-local.
- **Badge.** `ListView.tsx` reads only `sharing.lockedBy` (`sharingLockedBy`, string-typed and empty-guarded), draws `Locked by …` under `data-testid="sharing-locked-by"`, counts it in the toolbar's left-side layout, and imports neither `ViewSharingSchema` nor `Share2` any more. The test mounts a stored row still carrying `type: 'personal'` / `'collaborative'` and asserts no label and the lock drawn, which is the right behaviour for a served row the conversion has not yet rewritten. No other `ui/` consumer used the old `share-button` test id. `liveness/view.json` re-cites the row to `ListView.tsx#sharingLockedBy` and `Spec property liveness` is green.
- **Dogfood.** The head's `Dogfood Regression Gate (n/3)` shards are `skipped` because `ci.yml` runs them only off `pull_request` and `merge_group` events; the aggregate `success` verifies attestations, so the head's check-runs neither confirm nor deny the dev's local reds. Checked another way: #29365 (`dfbe34d8`, in the head) changes `packages/runtime` flow-start admission and its docs; #29451 (`6af3d295`, on `origin/main` but not in the head) re-points three `packages/qa/dogfood` flow pins. Neither touches a view path, and the merge queue's own run carries #29451. Every other check-run on the head is `success` or an opt-in `skipped`.
- **Docs and readers.** `view.mdx`, `protocol.mdx` and `object.mdx` are regenerated (`[REMOVED]` tombstone row for `type`, `scope` enum down to two members, the `owner` row re-worded off "parked direction"); `audience-based-interfaces.mdx:51` now says per-user list preferences. `git grep` on the head finds no server, objectql, services, cloud-connection, examples, templates or skills reader or writer of `scope: 'personal'`, `sharing.type` or `'collaborative'` in a view context; the only remaining spellings are the retirement kit, release-owned CHANGELOGs and the `content/docs/releases` pages the tree-scoped absence walk excludes by design. `main`'s ADR-0017 and ADR-0131 already carry the #28971 amendment notes (PR #29321, merged); ADR-0017's historic `z.enum(['package','shared','personal'])` line sits under that note and the card excludes the ADRs.
- **Residue, non-blocking, for a follow-up card:** `ui/packages/react/src/hooks/useViewSharing.ts` still says "aligned with ViewSharingSchema" over a four-value `visibility` enum and "Implements ViewSharingSchema from @objectstack/spec v2.0.7"; it is local component state with no reader or writer of either retired key, so it is not a stranded reader, but its docblock promises a spec alignment that has not existed for many majors. The dev's own out-of-scope notes (`view.manageShared` has no enforcing reader; `view.form.ts`'s `navigation_sharing` section describe) are pre-existing and correctly not folded into this PR.

### ④ Design judgment

- `view.zod.ts` against ruling C and the card: the narrowing takes nothing a consumer could use away. Both declarations were inert on `main` (both switcher read paths list every item bound to the object; the badge was the only reader), so the change makes the spec's refusal real where the old accept-set made a false visibility promise; the prescriptions name the version, the cause, the fix, the replacement (user-owned personal views) and the migrate command, with no tracker numbers in runtime strings. The docblocks now point to the ruling instead of a parked direction.
- `conversions/registry.ts` against its first consumers (`database-loader.ts`, `protocol-stored-item-conversion.ts`, `os migrate meta`, the artifact door): lossless by construction, copy-on-write, reach proven against every carrier, order and retirement stamp consistent with the chain.
- The `retired-keys` / `semantic` entries and the template fragment against ADR-0087: one D3 entry for two declarations that leave for one reason and share one replacement is a defensible single disposition; the value-level retirement has no `RETIRED_KEYS_BY_MAJOR` row, matching the `18.ui-form-view-type-layout-only` precedent, and the key-level one has its row. The D3 text states what the conversion cannot decide (keep, delete or rebuild the view) and its acceptance criteria are checkable.
- `normalize-list-view.ts` and `ListView.tsx` against the spec they consume: the emitter writes no retired key and the badge reads the one live key. A legacy-only pair now normalises to `sharing: {}` rather than being removed, which parses and draws nothing; harmless, noted.
- `@ts-expect-error` pins in the new test are compiled: `packages/spec`'s `typecheck` runs `check:test-typecheck` over the test files its `tsconfig.json` excludes, and the file is not in the debt ledger.

No must-fix found. The retirement is complete on every door, every stored shape converts, the declaration is consistent and at the right level, and the surface breach is exactly what the retirement forces.
